title: US government equity stakes in chip and chip-supply companies (Intel, xLight, SandboxAQ, I-Pulse, USA Rare Earth, quantum awards): terms, governance and returns
why_it_matters: Since August 2025 CHIPS money increasingly buys equity, warrants or royalties rather than paying grants; this turns the US government into a shareholder in the supply chain, with implications for governance, exits and competition.
questions: Which companies has Commerce taken equity, warrants or royalty rights in using CHIPS funds, with amounts, prices and dates?
What governance rights (voting agreements, board seats) come with the stakes?
What is the mark-to-market value of the stakes and has any been sold?
How do these deals compare with state equity models elsewhere (Japan Rapidus, China Big Fund, EU)?

title: Section 48D in practice: credits claimed, elective payments, who benefits and the extension fight after 2026
why_it_matters: The 48D credit (35% since 2026, cash-refundable) may now deliver more money to US fabs than CHIPS grants, but its realised cost and recipients are not reported, and its construction-start deadline expires at the end of 2026.
questions: How much 48D credit has been claimed and paid out by year?
Which companies disclose 48D receivables or refunds (Wolfspeed, TI, Micron, GlobalFoundries, Intel, TSMC Arizona)?
What bills propose extending or widening 48D and what are their scored costs?
How many projects began construction before the deadline via the 5% safe harbor?
